body.content: Counterfactual: What if the problem said 'The notebook costs $10 MORE EXPENSIVE than the pen' — does 'expensive' change anything? No, it's still additive. But what if it said '10 times as much'? Then n = 10p, p + 10p = 12.50, p = 12.50/11 ≈ 1.136. The additive vs multiplicative ambiguity is the key fork. In natural language, '$10 more' is almost always additive because of the dollar unit, but cross-linguistically this could differ.
body.why_keep_this: It clarifies why the standard reading is privileged: the unit-attached '$10' forces additive interpretation.
